title: Residential Electricity Supply: Utility Confirmation, Supply Start and Contract End Date
content:
Operations note, Residential Electricity Supply. After an enrollment is submitted, the utility either accepts it, recording the date of its confirmation letter as the utility confirmation date, or rejects it with one of the utility rejection reasons.

## Supply start

Supply begins on the switch meter read date, which becomes the service start date, and the agreement moves from enrollment pending to active. A rejected enrollment ends permanently, with the agreement status rejected; the customer may submit a new enrollment, which creates a new agreement and is priced on its own enrollment date. Neither confirmation nor activation changes the rate recorded at enrollment.

## Contract end date

For a plan whose term is above 0 months, the contract end date is the day before the same calendar day, term-months calendar months after the service start date. When that calendar day does not exist in the target month, the last day of that month is used before subtracting the day. A month-to-month plan has an empty contract end date.

| Service start date (hypothetical) | Term (months) | Same calendar day, term months later | Contract end date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-03-15 | 12 | 2026-03-15 | 2026-03-14 |
| 2025-01-01 | 6 | 2025-07-01 | 2025-06-30 |
| 2025-08-31 | 6 | 2026-02-31 does not exist, so 2026-02-28 is used | 2026-02-27 |
| 2024-05-31 | 24 | 2026-05-31 | 2026-05-30 |
| 2025-04-10 | 0 | not applicable | empty |

## Lifecycle at a glance

- enrollment pending, then active: the utility switches the premise to Beacon Ridge supply on the scheduled meter read date and electricity begins to flow under the agreement.
- enrollment pending, then rejected: the utility rejects the enrollment transaction and no supply ever starts.
